Alacrity

/uh-LAK-ruh-tee/ - the stress falls on LAK · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Alacrity means cheerful eagerness and promptness.

Asked who would lead the campus tour for the visiting families, Jae sprang up with alacrity, already reaching for the map bin.

Worked Example

When the food pantry's freezer failed at closing time, the manager asked whether anyone could drive the donations across town that night. Before she finished the sentence, Camila had the van keys in hand and was propping the door open, humming as she loaded the first crate.

Alacrity is more precise than eagerness or promptness alone because it names both at once - the quickness of the response and the visible cheerfulness behind it. Camila isn't just fast, and she isn't just willing; she is plainly delighted to be fast.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

eagerness: the desire itself, which can exist without quick action

promptness: speed alone, with no hint of enthusiasm

readiness: being prepared to act, not necessarily glad to

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reluctance: a dragging of the feet, wishing not to act

sluggishness: slowness of movement or response

Where it sits · how much delight rides on the speed — willingness → promptness → alacrity

willingness vs. alacrity: Willingness only means you won't refuse; you can be willing and still sigh, stall, and go last, while alacrity means you move first and gladly.

promptness vs. alacrity: Promptness gets you there on time with a neutral face; alacrity goes further, adding unmistakable delight to the speed.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — alacr-

Root — alacr-: lively, brisk

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of being

Put it together

Put it together: Alacr- (Latin alacer, 'lively, brisk') + -ity (the state of being) = the state of being briskly lively. Latin alacritas came into English almost unchanged. The same Latin alacer traveled into Italian as allegro, the musical instruction for 'brisk and cheerful' - so a musician playing allegro and a volunteer answering with alacrity are obeying the same ancient word.

Use the root in a new word: allegro

Use the root in a new word: allegro: The symphony's final movement is marked allegro, so the orchestra takes it at a brisk, cheerful pace.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Alacrity is a polished word for the everyday pairing of speed and cheer. In casual talk, 'eagerly' or 'right away' does the job; reach for alacrity when you want a single word to show that someone's quickness itself revealed their delight.
